ety.text: From Middle English biholden, from Old English behealdan (“to hold, possess, preserve, belong, keep, observe, look at, take care, beware, be cautious, restrain, act, behave”), from Proto-West Germanic *bihaldan (“to hold with, keep”), equivalent to be- + hold. chain.g: on the back side of, behind

ety.text: From Middle English behinde, behinden, from Old English behindan (“on the back side of, behind”), from Proto-West Germanic *bihindan, *bihindini (“on the back side of, in the rear of, behind”), from Proto-West Germanic *bi- + *hindō (“the hind side, back part”), equivalent to be- + hind. Compare Old Saxon bihindan (“behind”, adverb), Middle High German behinter (“behind; back”).

senses.d: At or to the back or far side of.
ex: The children were hiding behind the wall.
Behind the garage needs clearing asap.

senses.d: Concealed by (something serving as a facade or disguise).
ex: Behind the smile was a cruel intention.

senses.d: In the past, from the viewpoint of.
ex: All my problems are behind me.

senses.d: After in physical progress or distance.
ex: Smith finished the race a lap behind the others.
About the center, and a good way behind the rest, Silver and I followed — I tethered by my rope[…].

senses.d: After in developmental progress, score, grade, etc.; inferior to.
ex: I'm ranked sixth in the French class, behind five other pupils.
In the cricket match, England are 120 runs behind India.

senses.d: After in time.
ex: London is nine hours behind Tokyo.

senses.d: Responsible for, being the creator or controller of.
ex: Who is behind these terrorist attacks?
Mr Jones was the man behind the redevelopment plan.

senses.d: Underlying, being the reason for or explanation of.
ex: What is behind this unexpected decision?

senses.d: In support of.
ex: The republicans are fully behind their candidate.

senses.d: Following, subsequent to; as a result or consequence of; because of.
At or in the rear or back part of something.
ex: The water flows out through the pipe, and the sediment collects behind.

senses.d: In a rearward direction.
ex: We ran and ran, without once looking behind.

senses.d: So as to come after someone or something in position, distance, advancement, ranking, time, etc.
ex: The slower runners were left a long way behind.
In the cricket match, England finished a long way behind.

senses.d: So as to be still in place after someone or something has departed or ceased to exist.
ex: I couldn't be bothered to carry the ironing board, so I left it behind.
He stayed behind after the war.

senses.d: Backward in time or order of succession; past.
ex: […] forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before

senses.d: Behind the scenes in a theatre; backstage.
ex: ‘After the performance was over I went behind, and spoke to her.’

senses.d: Not yet brought forward, produced, or exhibited to view; out of sight; remaining.
ex: We cannot be sure that there is no evidence behind.

senses.d: Not advanced to the required or expected degree; overdue or in arrears.
ex: I'm very behind in my schedule.
My employer is two paychecks behind on paying my salary.

senses.d: Slow.
ex: My watch is behind by four minutes.

senses.d: The rear, back-end.
ex: This part fits under the behind of the vehicle.
She sneaked up on me from behind.

senses.d: The buttocks, bottom, butt.
ex: I was stung on the behind by a wasp.

senses.d: Synonym of ass (“synecdochic: a person or their body”).
ex: Get your lazy behind out of bed!

senses.d: A one-point score.
ex:
A roar from ten thousand throats go up,
For we've kicked another behind.
